Canadian Oil & Gas Producers Face Output Disruptions Amid Ongoing Workers' Walkout

Canada’s oil and gas production has been hit by a large-scale walkout by sector workers, as negotiations between labor unions and operator groups remain at an impasse. The industrial action, which began early Monday, has seen thousands of engineers, field technicians, and maintenance staff across Alberta, Saskatchewan, and British Columbia halt work at dozens of upstream facilities operated by companies including Northern Drilling Ltd and Prairie Resources Group.

The Canadian Oil & Gas Workers Union (COGWU) called the walkout after talks over wage increases and safety guarantees collapsed over the weekend. “Our members are committed to ensuring safe, sustainable operations, but their concerns have not been addressed. This action was a last resort,” said COGWU spokesman Derek Lamont. According to the union, more than 8,000 workers are participating in the strike.

Industry bodies report immediate reductions in production capacity, with the Western Canadian Basin particularly affected. According to the Canadian Association of Oil Producers (CAOP), up to 18% of the region’s daily crude output—around 650,000 barrels per day—has already been curtailed. “If a resolution isn’t reached soon, the impact on supply chains could deepen,” warned CAOP president Susan Blakely.

Northern Drilling Ltd confirmed that it has initiated shutdown protocols at several well sites, with non-unionized staff maintaining only essential safety operations. “We are prioritizing the safety of our assets and the environment,” the company said in a statement. Prairie Resources Group reported similar measures.

No timeline for resuming negotiations has been announced. “This is a critical moment for the industry,” said energy analyst Mark Duval of Resource Insight. “Extended disruptions could have significant repercussions for project timelines and operational costs.”

The situation remains fluid, with both sides expressing willingness to return to the bargaining table.
